certificate_authority_id.description: The user provided Resource ID for this Certificate Authority.
certificate_authority_id.rationale: Names the Certificate Authority; identifier values are organization-specific metadata.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Prevents destructive removal or unmanaged abandonment of a Certificate Authority.

deletion_protection.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the CertificateAuthority.
When the field is set to true or unset in Terraform state, a 'terraform apply'
or 'terraform destroy' that would delete the CertificateAuthority will fail.
When the field is set to false, deleting the CertificateAuthority is allowed.
deletion_protection.rationale: Prevents accidental or malicious CA deletion that would disrupt certificate issuance, revocation, and trust-chain operations.

desired_state.description:
Desired state of the CertificateAuthority. Set this field to 'STAGED' to create a 'STAGED' root CA.
Possible values: ENABLED, DISABLED, STAGED.
desired_state.rationale: Selects a valid CA lifecycle stage; no single state is universally secure.

gcs_bucket.description:
The name of a Cloud Storage bucket where this CertificateAuthority will publish content,
such as the CA certificate and CRLs. This must be a bucket name, without any prefixes
(such as 'gs://') or suffixes (such as '.googleapis.com'). For example, to use a bucket named
my-bucket, you would simply specify 'my-bucket'. If not specified, a managed bucket will be
created.
gcs_bucket.rationale: Selects a publication bucket whose access controls are assessed on the bucket resource.

ignore_active_certificates_on_deletion.description:
This field allows the CA to be deleted even if the CA has active certs. Active certs include both unrevoked and unexpired certs.
Use with care. Defaults to 'false'.
ignore_active_certificates_on_deletion.rationale: Allows deletion despite active certificates, bypassing a CA safety control.

labels.description:
Labels with user-defined metadata.

An object containing a list of "key": value pairs. Example: { "name": "wrench", "mass":
"1.3kg", "count": "3" }.


**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Stores user-defined metadata and does not change CA security behavior.

lifetime.description:
The desired lifetime of the CA certificate. Used to create the "notBeforeTime" and
"notAfterTime" fields inside an X.509 certificate. A duration in seconds with up to nine
fractional digits, terminated by 's'. Example: "3.5s".
lifetime.rationale: CA lifetime is specific to the PKI hierarchy and certificate rotation design.

location.description:
Location of the CertificateAuthority. A full list of valid locations can be found by
running 'gcloud privateca locations list'.
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

pem_ca_certificate.description: The signed CA certificate issued from the subordinated CA's CSR. This is needed when activating the subordiante CA with a third party issuer.
pem_ca_certificate.rationale: Contains an issuer-specific signed certificate that cannot be generically constrained as text.

pool.description: The name of the CaPool this Certificate Authority belongs to.
pool.rationale: References a CA pool, whose security posture is assessed on the pool resource.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Selects the owning project rather than configuring a CA security control.

skip_grace_period.description:
If this flag is set, the Certificate Authority will be deleted as soon as
possible without a 30-day grace period where undeletion would have been
allowed. If you proceed, there will be no way to recover this CA.
Use with care. Defaults to 'false'.
skip_grace_period.rationale: Removes the CA recovery period and permits irreversible deletion immediately.

type.description:
The Type of this CertificateAuthority.

~> **Note:** For 'SUBORDINATE' Certificate Authorities, they need to
be activated before they can issue certificates. Default value: "SELF_SIGNED" Possible values: ["SELF_SIGNED", "SUBORDINATE"]
type.rationale: Root versus subordinate CA is a valid PKI architecture choice.

config.description: The config used to create a self-signed X.509 certificate or CSR.

config.subject_config.description: Specifies some of the values in a certificate that are related to the subject.

config.subject_config.subject.description: Contains distinguished name fields such as the location and organization.

config.subject_config.subject.common_nam.description: The common name of the distinguished name.
config.subject_config.subject.common_nam.rationale: Distinguished-name identity is specific to the organization and CA profile.

config.subject_config.subject.country_co.description: The country code of the subject.
config.subject_config.subject.country_co.rationale: Distinguished-name identity is specific to the organization and CA profile.

config.subject_config.subject.locality.description: The locality or city of the subject.
config.subject_config.subject.locality.rationale: Distinguished-name identity is specific to the organization and CA profile.

config.subject_config.subject.organizati.rationale: Distinguished-name identity is specific to the organization and CA profile.

config.subject_config.subject.organizati.description: The organizational unit of the subject.
config.subject_config.subject.organizati.rationale: Distinguished-name identity is specific to the organization and CA profile.

config.subject_config.subject.postal_cod.description: The postal code of the subject.
config.subject_config.subject.postal_cod.rationale: Distinguished-name identity is specific to the organization and CA profile.

config.subject_config.subject.province.description: The province, territory, or regional state of the subject.
config.subject_config.subject.province.rationale: Distinguished-name identity is specific to the organization and CA profile.

config.subject_config.subject.street_add.description: The street address of the subject.
config.subject_config.subject.street_add.rationale: Distinguished-name identity is specific to the organization and CA profile.

config.subject_config.subject_alt_name.d.description: Contains only valid, fully-qualified host names.
config.subject_config.subject_alt_name.d.rationale: CA subject identities are deployment-specific and cannot use a generic allowlist.

config.subject_config.subject_alt_name.e.description: Contains only valid RFC 2822 E-mail addresses.
config.subject_config.subject_alt_name.e.rationale: CA subject identities are deployment-specific and cannot use a generic allowlist.

config.subject_config.subject_alt_name.i.description: Contains only valid 32-bit IPv4 addresses or RFC 4291 IPv6 addresses.
config.subject_config.subject_alt_name.i.rationale: CA subject identities are deployment-specific and cannot use a generic allowlist.

config.subject_config.subject_alt_name.u.rationale: CA subject identities are deployment-specific and cannot use a generic allowlist.

config.subject_key_id.description: When specified this provides a custom SKI to be used in the certificate. This should only be used to maintain a SKI of an existing CA originally created outside CA service, which was not generated using method (1) described in RFC 5280 section 4.2.1.2..

config.subject_key_id.key_id.description: The value of the KeyId in lowercase hexadecimal.
config.subject_key_id.key_id.rationale: A custom subject key identifier supports external-CA migration and is CA-specific.

config.x509_config.description: Describes how some of the technical X.509 fields in a certificate should be populated.

config.x509_config.aia_ocsp_servers.description:
Describes Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) endpoint addresses that appear in the
"Authority Information Access" extension in the certificate.
config.x509_config.aia_ocsp_servers.rationale: OCSP endpoint values are PKI-specific and have no universal URL allowlist.

config.x509_config.additional_extensions.description: Specifies an X.509 extension, which may be used in different parts of X.509 objects like certificates, CSRs, and CRLs.

Indicates whether or not this extension is critical (i.e., if the client does not know how to
handle this extension, the client should consider this to be an error).
config.x509_config.additional_extensions.rationale: Criticality depends on the semantics of the specific custom X.509 extension.

config.x509_config.additional_extensions.description: The value of this X.509 extension. A base64-encoded string.
config.x509_config.additional_extensions.rationale: Custom base64 extension content is PKI-profile-specific and cannot be generically constrained.

config.x509_config.additional_extensions.description: Describes values that are relevant in a CA certificate.
An ObjectId specifies an object identifier (OID). These provide context and describe types in ASN.1 messages.
config.x509_config.additional_extensions.rationale: Custom extension OIDs are application and PKI-profile-specific.

config.x509_config.ca_options.description: Describes values that are relevant in a CA certificate.

config.x509_config.ca_options.is_ca.description: When true, the "CA" in Basic Constraints extension will be set to true.
config.x509_config.ca_options.is_ca.rationale: The service requires a valid CA certificate configuration, making an additional generic policy redundant.

config.x509_config.ca_options.max_issuer.description:
Refers to the "path length constraint" in Basic Constraints extension. For a CA certificate, this value describes the depth of
subordinate CA certificates that are allowed. If this value is less than 0, the request will fail. Setting the value to 0
requires setting 'zero_max_issuer_path_length = true'.
config.x509_config.ca_options.max_issuer.rationale: Permitted subordinate depth depends on the designed PKI hierarchy.

config.x509_config.ca_options.non_ca.description:
When true, the "CA" in Basic Constraints extension will be set to false.
If both 'is_ca' and 'non_ca' are unset, the extension will be omitted from the CA certificate.
config.x509_config.ca_options.non_ca.rationale: The service requires a valid CA certificate configuration, making an additional generic policy redundant.

config.x509_config.ca_options.zero_max_i.description:
When true, the "path length constraint" in Basic Constraints extension will be set to 0.
If both 'max_issuer_path_length' and 'zero_max_issuer_path_length' are unset,
the max path length will be omitted from the CA certificate.
config.x509_config.ca_options.zero_max_i.rationale: Permitted subordinate depth depends on the designed PKI hierarchy.

config.x509_config.key_usage.description: Indicates the intended use for keys that correspond to a certificate.

config.x509_config.key_usage.base_key_us.description: Describes high-level ways in which a key may be used.
The key may be used to sign certificates.
config.x509_config.key_usage.base_key_us.rationale: CA-required key usage is validated by the service and does not need a duplicate policy.

config.x509_config.key_usage.base_key_us.description: The key may be used for cryptographic commitments. Note that this may also be referred to as "non-repudiation".
config.x509_config.key_usage.base_key_us.rationale: Additional key usages depend on the certificate profile and interoperability requirements.

config.x509_config.key_usage.base_key_us.description: The key may be used sign certificate revocation lists.
config.x509_config.key_usage.base_key_us.rationale: CA-required key usage is validated by the service and does not need a duplicate policy.

config.x509_config.key_usage.base_key_us.description: The key may be used to encipher data.
config.x509_config.key_usage.base_key_us.rationale: Additional key usages depend on the certificate profile and interoperability requirements.

config.x509_config.key_usage.base_key_us.description: The key may be used to decipher only.
config.x509_config.key_usage.base_key_us.rationale: Additional key usages depend on the certificate profile and interoperability requirements.

config.x509_config.key_usage.base_key_us.description: The key may be used for digital signatures.
config.x509_config.key_usage.base_key_us.rationale: Additional key usages depend on the certificate profile and interoperability requirements.

config.x509_config.key_usage.base_key_us.description: The key may be used to encipher only.
config.x509_config.key_usage.base_key_us.rationale: Additional key usages depend on the certificate profile and interoperability requirements.

config.x509_config.key_usage.base_key_us.description: The key may be used in a key agreement protocol.
config.x509_config.key_usage.base_key_us.rationale: Additional key usages depend on the certificate profile and interoperability requirements.

config.x509_config.key_usage.base_key_us.description: The key may be used to encipher other keys.
config.x509_config.key_usage.base_key_us.rationale: Additional key usages depend on the certificate profile and interoperability requirements.

config.x509_config.key_usage.extended_ke.description: Describes high-level ways in which a key may be used.
Corresponds to OID 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.2. Officially described as "TLS WWW client authentication", though regularly used for non-WWW TLS.
config.x509_config.key_usage.extended_ke.rationale: Extended key usages are PKI use-case-specific and have no universal combination.

config.x509_config.key_usage.extended_ke.description: Corresponds to OID 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.3. Officially described as "Signing of downloadable executable code client authentication".
config.x509_config.key_usage.extended_ke.rationale: Extended key usages are PKI use-case-specific and have no universal combination.

config.x509_config.key_usage.extended_ke.description: Corresponds to OID 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.4. Officially described as "Email protection".
config.x509_config.key_usage.extended_ke.rationale: Extended key usages are PKI use-case-specific and have no universal combination.

config.x509_config.key_usage.extended_ke.description: Corresponds to OID 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.9. Officially described as "Signing OCSP responses".
config.x509_config.key_usage.extended_ke.rationale: Extended key usages are PKI use-case-specific and have no universal combination.

config.x509_config.key_usage.extended_ke.description: Corresponds to OID 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.1. Officially described as "TLS WWW server authentication", though regularly used for non-WWW TLS.
config.x509_config.key_usage.extended_ke.rationale: Extended key usages are PKI use-case-specific and have no universal combination.

config.x509_config.key_usage.extended_ke.description: Corresponds to OID 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.8. Officially described as "Binding the hash of an object to a time".
config.x509_config.key_usage.extended_ke.rationale: Extended key usages are PKI use-case-specific and have no universal combination.

config.x509_config.key_usage.unknown_ext.description: An ObjectId specifies an object identifier (OID). These provide context and describe types in ASN.1 messages.
An ObjectId specifies an object identifier (OID). These provide context and describe types in ASN.1 messages.
config.x509_config.key_usage.unknown_ext.rationale: Custom extended-key-usage OIDs are specific to the PKI profile.

config.x509_config.name_constraints.description: Describes the X.509 name constraints extension.

config.x509_config.name_constraints.crit.description: Indicates whether or not the name constraints are marked critical.
config.x509_config.name_constraints.crit.rationale: Makes X.509 name constraints fail closed for clients that cannot process them.

config.x509_config.name_constraints.excl.description:
Contains excluded DNS names. Any DNS name that can be
constructed by simply adding zero or more labels to
the left-hand side of the name satisfies the name constraint.
For example, 'example.com', 'www.example.com', 'www.sub.example.com'
would satisfy 'example.com' while 'example1.com' does not.
config.x509_config.name_constraints.excl.rationale: Allowed and excluded namespaces are specific to the organization and PKI profile.

config.x509_config.name_constraints.excl.description:
Contains the excluded email addresses. The value can be a particular
email address, a hostname to indicate all email addresses on that host or
a domain with a leading period (e.g. '.example.com') to indicate
all email addresses in that domain.
config.x509_config.name_constraints.excl.rationale: Allowed and excluded namespaces are specific to the organization and PKI profile.

config.x509_config.name_constraints.excl.description:
Contains the excluded IP ranges. For IPv4 addresses, the ranges
are expressed using CIDR notation as specified in RFC 4632.
For IPv6 addresses, the ranges are expressed in similar encoding as IPv4
addresses.
config.x509_config.name_constraints.excl.rationale: Allowed and excluded namespaces are specific to the organization and PKI profile.

config.x509_config.name_constraints.excl.description:
Contains the excluded URIs that apply to the host part of the name.
The value can be a hostname or a domain with a
leading period (like '.example.com')
config.x509_config.name_constraints.excl.rationale: Allowed and excluded namespaces are specific to the organization and PKI profile.

config.x509_config.name_constraints.perm.description:
Contains permitted DNS names. Any DNS name that can be
constructed by simply adding zero or more labels to
the left-hand side of the name satisfies the name constraint.
For example, 'example.com', 'www.example.com', 'www.sub.example.com'
would satisfy 'example.com' while 'example1.com' does not.
config.x509_config.name_constraints.perm.rationale: Allowed and excluded namespaces are specific to the organization and PKI profile.

config.x509_config.name_constraints.perm.description:
Contains the permitted email addresses. The value can be a particular
email address, a hostname to indicate all email addresses on that host or
a domain with a leading period (e.g. '.example.com') to indicate
all email addresses in that domain.
config.x509_config.name_constraints.perm.rationale: Allowed and excluded namespaces are specific to the organization and PKI profile.

config.x509_config.name_constraints.perm.description:
Contains the permitted IP ranges. For IPv4 addresses, the ranges
are expressed using CIDR notation as specified in RFC 4632.
For IPv6 addresses, the ranges are expressed in similar encoding as IPv4
addresses.
config.x509_config.name_constraints.perm.rationale: Allowed and excluded namespaces are specific to the organization and PKI profile.

config.x509_config.name_constraints.perm.description:
Contains the permitted URIs that apply to the host part of the name.
The value can be a hostname or a domain with a
leading period (like '.example.com')
config.x509_config.name_constraints.perm.rationale: Allowed and excluded namespaces are specific to the organization and PKI profile.

config.x509_config.policy_ids.description: Describes the X.509 certificate policy object identifiers, per https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5280#section-4.2.1.4.

config.x509_config.policy_ids.object_id_.description: An ObjectId specifies an object identifier (OID). These provide context and describe types in ASN.1 messages.
config.x509_config.policy_ids.object_id_.rationale: Certificate-policy OIDs identify organization-specific PKI policies.

key_spec.description:
Used when issuing certificates for this CertificateAuthority. If this CertificateAuthority
is a self-signed CertificateAuthority, this key is also used to sign the self-signed CA
certificate. Otherwise, it is used to sign a CSR.

key_spec.algorithm.description:
The algorithm to use for creating a managed Cloud KMS key for a for a simplified
experience. All managed keys will be have their ProtectionLevel as HSM. Possible values: ["SIGN_HASH_ALGORITHM_UNSPECIFIED", "RSA_PSS_2048_SHA256", "RSA_PSS_3072_SHA256", "RSA_PSS_4096_SHA256", "RSA_PKCS1_2048_SHA256", "RSA_PKCS1_3072_SHA256", "RSA_PKCS1_4096_SHA256", "EC_P256_SHA256", "EC_P384_SHA384"]
key_spec.algorithm.rationale: Controls the strength of the CA signing key; requiring approved algorithms prevents weak cryptographic signatures.

key_spec.cloud_kms_key_version.description:
The resource name for an existing Cloud KMS CryptoKeyVersion in the format
'projects/*/locations/*/keyRings/*/cryptoKeys/*/cryptoKeyVersions/*'.
key_spec.cloud_kms_key_version.rationale: References a KMS key version whose algorithm, rotation, and IAM are assessed on that resource.

subordinate_config.description:
If this is a subordinate CertificateAuthority, this field will be set
with the subordinate configuration, which describes its issuers.

subordinate_config.certificate_authority.description:
This can refer to a CertificateAuthority that was used to create a
subordinate CertificateAuthority. This field is used for information
and usability purposes only. The resource name is in the format
'projects/*/locations/*/caPools/*/certificateAuthorities/*'.
subordinate_config.certificate_authority.rationale: References a parent CA whose trust and security posture are assessed independently.

subordinate_config.pem_issuer_chain.description:
Contains the PEM certificate chain for the issuers of this CertificateAuthority,
but not pem certificate for this CA itself.

subordinate_config.pem_issuer_chain.pem_.description: Expected to be in leaf-to-root order according to RFC 5246.
subordinate_config.pem_issuer_chain.pem_.rationale: Issuer-chain content is hierarchy-specific and cryptographically validated.

user_defined_access_urls.description:
Custom URLs for accessing content published by this CA, such as the CA certificate and CRLs,
that can be specified by users.

user_defined_access_urls.aia_issuing_cer.description: A list of URLs where this CertificateAuthority's CA certificate is published that is specified by users.
user_defined_access_urls.aia_issuing_cer.rationale: Certificate publication endpoints are deployment-specific and have no universal hostname allowlist.

user_defined_access_urls.crl_access_urls.description: A list of URLs where this CertificateAuthority's CRLs are published that is specified by users.
user_defined_access_urls.crl_access_urls.rationale: CRL publication endpoints are deployment-specific and have no universal hostname allowlist.
